text:
Riya: FYI I'm opening a lightweight PR to roll up the various call-shape examples into one 'call patterns' landing doc. Intention: one canonical place for function/tool calling, with language-specific snippets and a short migration recipe. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/927 :wave:
Tom: Nice. Can we include Go + Ruby snippets too? Most of our examples are TS/Python heavy and some customers asked for Go idioms.
Riya: Yes — planning to add tiny Go and Ruby variants. They'll be minimal, just the typed response handling and a note about nullable lists.
Evan: Heads-up on anchors: some legacy blog posts link to headings that get tokenized differently by the markdown renderer. I suggest adding a redirect table near the top of the page and also update the table-of-contents anchors.
Marisol: I'll run the snippet linter after you push. Last time there was an issue where the Ruby example used `||=` in a way that hides nil vs empty array semantics. We should show an explicit normalization step.
Riya: Good point. For Ruby I'll do `items = resp['items'] || []` and add a note explaining the behavior for `nil` vs `[]`.
Tom: For Go we should show `if resp.Items == nil { resp.Items = []string{} }` — explicit is clearer than panics or nil derefs.
Evan: Also adding a tiny CI check to detect broken internal anchors. Simple grep across generated HTML for hrefs that start with "#" and ensure targets exist. I'll open a separate PR for that test.
Riya: Can you also add a small migration snippet that maps old shape keys? Some folks still parse `tool.name` and `tool.args` directly. We should show a 3-line shim.
Marisol: Example shim suggestion for the docs (pseudo-code): `func MapLegacyToolCall(msg map[string]interface{}) map[string]interface{} { if t, ok := msg["tool"].(map[string]interface{}); ok { return map[string]interface{}{"function": t["name"], "params": t["arguments"]} } return msg }` — short and shows mapping.
Tom: For JS/TS I'll add an idiomatic normalization: `const out = resp.items ?? [] // normalize nullable list` and show `/** prefer client.call() wrapper over raw fetch for examples */` so we keep examples consistent.
Evan: I'll prepare the redirect table with three columns: legacy-anchor, current-anchor, notes. We'll commit it to the doc and add a comment telling editors to update it when headings change.
Riya: Who can sanity-check the anchors? I want someone to run the local renderer and click the links before merge.
Marisol: I'm on it. After you push I'll run `yarn docs:build` locally and then hit all internal anchors with a quick script. Will report back.
ci-bot: PR #927 opened by Riya — CI queued. (auto)
Tom: Also check code block captions — the linter flagged a missing caption in the Python snippet last week. I'll add a one-line caption for each code block to satisfy the lint rules.
Marisol: Local lint run now: two nits — missing caption (Tom will fix) and the Ruby `||` note needs clarification (Riya will add).
Riya: Pushed updates: added Go + Ruby snippets, migration shim, redirect table, and short note about caption style. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/927/files
ci-bot: Snippet tests for PR #927 running... (auto)
Marisol: Quick review: Go snippet uses `resp.Items = make([]string, 0)` when nil, good. Ruby normalization shows explicit `items = resp['items'] || []`. Python snippet caption added.
Evan: Opened the anchor-check test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/930 — tiny grep-based test, fails loudly with a helpful message identifying the broken anchor.
ci-bot: PR #930 created by Evan — CI queued. (auto)
ci-bot: PR #927 snippet tests passed, doc build OK. (auto)
Riya: Great — merging #927. Evan, can you merge the anchor test after a quick review? I want that test in master before we touch other pages.
Evan: Will do in ~20m. Also adding a small CONTRIBUTING note in the doc about updating redirect table if headings are renamed.
Tom: Thx all. Small wins for cross-language coverage and fewer broken links.
Marisol: Verified final smoke: anchors and snippets pass. Logging results in the PR.
Riya: Thanks team! :tada:
